The supply of food in every country all the time is less than the demand. So money has to pay for getting food, i.e. it means the insufficiency of food. Its characteristics include: prohibition of interest (riba), compulsory charity (Zakat), emphasis on ethical and fair trade, recognition of private ownership within Islamic limits, and the goal of achieving social justice and economic welfare.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Which one of the above mentioned systems doesn’t permit freedom of the consumers? Describe.","marks":4,"answer":"From the above-mentioned economic system, the socialist economic system doesn’t permit freedom of the consumers. In a socialist economic system, the ownership of the factory of production, production process, and distribution of produced assets is different, compared to a capitalistic system. All assets including factors of production are under state ownership in the socialist economic system. No private ownership is vested in the asset. The government makes basic decisions in producing goods and imparting services to the citizens in a socialistic economic system. There is no freedom in making decisions regarding production by the producer in the socialist economic system. Similarly, the consumer has no privilege to consume goods according to their own wish. The producers grow foods determined by the government, and the consumers purchase and consume these according to the need. The consumers enjoy the freedom to select necessary goods and purchase socially. In the socialistic economic system, all economic activities are conducted to meet the basic needs of each citizen and to attain the highest welfare for the people. There is no scope here for earning personal profit. So, a socialist economic system doesn’t permit the freedom of the consumers.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Moreover, any qualifying characteristics of a citizen of a country such as skills, creative power, technical knowledge, financial assets, gold, silver, factories, machineries, state owned vehicles, educational institutions, roads and streets, bridges and culverts, hospitals, important buildings, monuments, forests and many natural resources fall under the category of national resources. [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is an International Resource?","marks":1,"answer":"Resources that do not belong to any state rather can be enjoyed by every nation in the world are called International Resources.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the sources of National Resources.","marks":2,"answer":"The sources of National Resources are:
Personal Resources: Assets owned by individuals such as land, house, money, car, factory, etc.
Collective Resources: Assets owned collectively by the society or the state, such as roads, railways, parks, government hospitals, schools, forests, rivers, minerals, etc.
Human Capital: Skills, knowledge, creativity, and technical expertise of citizens.
Together, all personal resources of citizens and all collective resources constitute the national resources of a country.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the concept of resource in Economic terms rather than in light of Siraj’s statement.","marks":3,"answer":"In economic terms, a resource is defined as anything that has utility (ability to satisfy a want), scarcity (limited supply relative to demand), visibility (can be seen or measured), and transferability (can be transferred from one person to another). Examples include land, labor, capital, machinery, raw materials, etc. Siraj’s statement (“Love of the customers is my real asset”) reflects a moral or social asset (goodwill), but in strict economics, goodwill lacks scarcity, visibility, and easy transferability, so it is not classified as an economic resource.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Is the goodwill of Siraj’s business a resource? Analyze the opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"No, the goodwill of Siraj’s business is not considered a resource in economics. Although goodwill has utility (it attracts customers and increases sales), it lacks the other essential characteristics of an economic resource:
Scarcity: Goodwill is not inherently scarce in the same way physical goods are.
Visibility: It is an intangible asset, not physically visible.
Transferability: While business goodwill can sometimes be sold with a business, its transfer is complex and not as straightforward as tangible assets.
Therefore, from a strict economics perspective, goodwill is not classified as a resource. However, in business and accounting, it is recognized as an intangible asset that adds value to a firm.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is labor?","marks":1,"answer":"The physical and mental abilities of a man usable in production work are referred to as labor.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the stages of economic functions.","marks":2,"answer":"The various stages of economic functions are —
Want → Effort → Production → Distribution → Consumption
People perform various economic functions to fulfill different kinds of needs and wants. The need or desire for any goods or services is known as want. People make efforts to fulfill their various needs and wants. With the four factors of production i.e. land, labor, capital and organization, people conduct different production processes. The produced assets are distributed among the said four factors of production. Lastly, the process of consumption takes place.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"What kind of resource is the premises mentioned in the stem? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The premises mentioned in the stem i.e. Shahid Minar is one kind of collective resource. Resources which are enjoyed collectively by all the people in a society are known as collective resources or assets. All the citizens of the country have equal rights on and equal obligations to this kind of assets. Roads, railways, embankments, parks, government hospitals, schools, monuments and all the natural resources under state ownership such as forests, mineral resources and rivers are collective resources. We learn from the stem that on Ekushey February, a painting competition was held at the premises of Shahid Minar. This premises is a collective resource. In 1952, the Bengalis in the then East Pakistan vigorously participated in the language movement to defend the honor of their mother language, Bangla. During a protest on 21 February, the police openly fired on the protesters, killing Abul Barkat, Jabbar, Rafique and Salam and injuring many others. To pay tribute to these martyrs and immortalize their contributions, Shahid Minar (memorial) was built and erected in front of Dhaka Medical College. On 21 February every year, people pay tribute to the language martyrs by laying wreaths at the monument. This is not a private property. All the citizens of the country have equal rights on and equal obligations to Shahid Minar. This is why, the premises in the stem i.e. Shahid Minar is a collective resource.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Will Roshan’s talent be considered a resource? Analyze with logics.","marks":4,"answer":"Originally, Roshan’s painting talent in the stem is one kind of mental asset. However, because his talent has not been used to earn money, it cannot be considered a resource in economics. Usually, resources mean land, house, various types of necessary and durable goods, gold, silver etc. Though, in general, any materials or objects essential for humans can be called resources, from the perspective of economics, not every material or object is a resource. For a material to be considered a resource from the perspective of economics, it must have utility, insufficiency, visibility and exchangeability. In the stem, we learn about Roshan who won the first place in the painting competition held at the premises of Shahid Minar on Ekushey February. Because of his amazing painting skill, the story of sacrifices of the language martyrs was so beautifully reflected in his creation that it moved everyone present in the ceremony. This talent of Roshan cannot be considered a resource in economics mainly because it is not transferrable. However, if Roshan can produce resources by utilizing his skill, it will be considered a personal asset. Another similar example is health. A person’s health has the characteristics of utility and insufficiency but because it lacks visibility and exchangeability, it cannot be called a resource. However, if a healthy person can earn money by capitalizing on his physical health, it will be considered a resource. Therefore, it can be concluded that since Roshan’s painting talent has not been used to earn money, it cannot be considered as a resource from the perspective of economics.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is the utility?","marks":1,"answer":"The ability to fulfill the need of any commodity is called utility.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why it is necessary to preserve collective resources?","marks":2,"answer":"It is very important to preserve our resources by ensuring their proper use. Roads, bridges, hospitals, schools, and public transportation (such as – buses, trains, and motor launches) fall under state-owned resources. Natural resources (such as – forests, and mineral resources) are known as collective resources. The state ensures the development and welfare of the people by proper usage of these resources. Therefore, it is the responsibility of every citizen of the country to preserve collective resources through their proper use.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the economic characteristics of X country.","marks":3,"answer":"The capitalist economic system exists in country ‘X’. In the capitalistic economic system, the individual alone or collectively conducts the production activities. Entrepreneurs can produce goods according to their wishes. Similarly, consumers have the privilege to consume goods according to their will. The price of the product is determined through competition among the buyers and sellers. The main characteristic of this economic system is that factors of production are under individual ownership. It is such a system where personal or private initiatives are given preference. Here, an individual can produce, trade, and consume according to his/her wish. Producers and consumers have full freedom. The most important characteristic of this system is that here an individual or producer invests and conducts the production process for earning maximum profit. The producers invest more money for such goods that have the possibility of making more profit. To earn maximum profit, the capitalists try to give fewer wages to the laborers than the just wage. As a result, a vast amount of assets are accumulated in the hands of a small number of capitalists and entrepreneurs. In this way, the disparity of assets is created in society.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Compare the economic characteristics of X and Y country.","marks":4,"answer":"The economic system of X is a capitalistic economic system and the economic system of Y country is a socialistic economic system. In a capitalist system, individuals and businesses own the means of production, such as factories, land, and capital. The market forces of supply and demand determine prices and resource allocation. Businesses strive to maximize profits, which drives innovation and efficiency. The government’s role is generally limited to providing a legal framework and regulating markets. Capitalism can lead to significant economic inequality, as wealth and income tend to concentrate in the hands of a few. In contrast, socialism emphasizes state or collective ownership of the means of production. The government plays a central role in planning and coordinating economic activity. Social welfare and equality are prioritized, with the government providing essential services such as healthcare and education. Competition is often restricted, and economic inequality is aimed to be reduced by distributing wealth and resources more equitably. While capitalism and socialism represent distinct economic models, many countries have adopted mixed economies that combine elements of both systems. For example, the United States, primarily a capitalist economy, has social welfare programs like Social Security and Medicare. Similarly, China, once predominantly socialist, has embraced market reforms and incorporated capitalist elements into its economy.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called economic system?","marks":1,"answer":"An economic system, is a system of production, resource allocation and distribution of goods and services within a society or a given geographic area.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"How can we preserve our national resource?","marks":2,"answer":"We can preserve our national resources by keeping them secure and making sure that they are not damaged through cautionary steps. The individual resources of all the citizens of the country and the collective resources of society together are called national resources. National resources need to be preserved for the benefit of the state, society, and citizens. Firstly, we have to ensure that no one is damaging the national resources, and if anyone does, we should inform the authorities. Secondly, we must not waste our national resources. Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Scenario-1 reflects the Islamic economic system. The economic and all functions are run in Islamic economic system as per the provision of Sariah. Since exploitation free production system is followed in the Islamic economic system, the paying of remuneration on the basis of equity and justice is ensured. Components are paid based on one’s contribution to production. There is the arrangement of paying just dues to the labourers in time in this economic system. Moreover, a certain amount of money from the dividends is arranged to be distributed. As a result, the proper distribution of produced asset is possible. In the stimulus scene-1, it can be observed that Mr. Golap, residing in country ‘B’, owns two factories. He pays the workers properly. Besides, he distributed a certain amount of money from the dividend among the poor. These activities of Mr. Golap are similar to the Islamic economic system. Because, in this system, apart from paying wages to the workers properly or as an incentive, a part of the dividend is given to the poor. Hence, it can be said that the Islamic economic system is indicated in scenario-1.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Economic system of whose country is the best? Show logic after identifying the economic systems of the country of Mr. Rafiq and Mr. Razzak.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. Rafiq’s country’s economic system is better than that of the country of Mr. Razzak. Mr. Rafiq lives in a Muslim country where the Islamic economic system is maintained. Therefore, the Sariah is considered the law. Although he can do business as he likes without the restrictions imposed upon him by the government, he is not entirely free to consume as much as he wants. There are strict rules, which provide him with an outline that helps society stay balanced. Mr. Razzak, on the other hand, lives in a country where he cannot do business as he pleases. His business and other activities are controlled by the state. This refers to a socialist economic system. I think the Islamic economic system is better than the socialist economic system because the socialist economic system considers the state to be the owner of all resources, while the Islamic economic system acknowledges self-ownership. The Islamic economic system still considers the necessity of economic balance and therefore imposes laws to ensure that the rich cannot get very rich and that they help the poor. Also, the Islamic economic system ensures that no haram production is taking place, but this is not guaranteed in a socialist state. Explain at least two characteristics in detail.","marks":3,"answer":"The production system indicated in the scenario is a capitalist or free-market economy. In this type of economic system, individuals and private businesses have the freedom to produce, distribute, and consume goods and services with minimal government intervention. Here are two key characteristics of a capitalist production system:
Ownership of Components of Production: The components such as land, labor, capital, and organization are under individual ownership in the capitalistic economic system. It means that the individual achieves the ownership of land with the help of his assets or income. The individual can consume and transfer freely his own assets and make all the decisions.
Freedom to Take Initiatives: The individual alone or collectively can take any initiative for producing goods or services in the capitalist economic system and can make necessary investments. In this case, there is no restriction. The capitalistic economy is often called many times as free market economy. In this economic system, production, distribution, and consumption of goods are operated based on demand and supply. The main characteristic of a capitalist system is the independence to make decisions by the individual. It can be said that there is no interference of government in this case.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"There are huge differences in the production system of scenario-1 and scenario-2-Explain four differences to support the statement.","marks":4,"answer":"Scenario 1, a capitalistic economy is represented, seen in countries like America, the UK, Germany, and Japan, where individuals and businesses enjoy freedom in production, distribution, and consumption. In Scenario 2, a socialistic economy is depicted, as in China and Cuba, where the government controls production, limiting individual economic freedom. Four key differences:
Ownership: Capitalism features private ownership of means of production; Socialism features state/collective ownership.
Economic Freedom: Capitalism allows full freedom for producers and consumers; Socialism severely restricts individual economic freedom, with state making all key decisions.
Profit Motive: The primary driving force in capitalism is profit maximization; in socialism, it is social welfare and need fulfillment.
Price Determination: In capitalism, prices are determined by market forces of supply and demand; in socialism, prices are often set by the state.

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is meant by the prosperity of a country?","marks":1,"answer":"The prosperity of a country refers to its overall economic well-being, characterized by high standards of living, equitable distribution of wealth, full employment, and social welfare for all citizens.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"\"A country that is rich in national resources is more likely to prosper\"—Analyze the statement.","marks":2,"answer":"The statement \"A country that is rich in national resources is more likely to prosper\" is largely true. National resources (both natural and human) form the foundation for economic activities. Abundant resources can fuel industrialization, generate revenue, create jobs, and support infrastructure development. However, prosperity also depends on effective management, good governance, technological advancement, and fair distribution of resource benefits. A resource-rich country without proper management may not achieve prosperity.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which economic system is present in Jim's country? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Jim's country has a socialist economic system. The description that everyone gets work according to ability, is paid according to work, and there is no unemployment aligns with socialist principles where the state ensures full employment and distributes income based on contribution.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Do you think it is possible to build a non-exploitative society through the socialist economic system of Jim's country? Give your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"Yes, I think it is possible to build a non-exploitative society through the socialist economic system of Jim's country. An economic system in which all economic activities are conducted with the aim of meeting the basic needs of every citizen and achieving the overall welfare of the people is called a socialist economic system. One of the traits of this system is that everyone will get work according to their ability and will get paid according to their work. There is no unemployment in this system. Although income varies according to eligibility, no one is deprived of income according to their contribution. These features are also observed in the stem in Jim's country. So, the socialist economic system is present in this country. In a socialist economy, the country lets everyone work according to their ability and qualifications. Although the income of all is not the same, no one is deprived of it according to their contribution to production. Due to these chances, there is not a balanced distribution of the acquired wealth's income. Inequality in such an economy is much lower than in a mixed economy. In a socialist economy, the activities of production, distribution, and consumption are done according to the needs of the people. As all economic activities are managed by the state under a central plan, wastage of resources is also relatively low. As a result, the gross national product also increases gradually, and the balance of resources is properly distributed. From the above discussion, it appears that the socialist economic system is governed by the principle of balanced distribution. An exploitation-free society can be developed in this system, as it is managed by the state for the welfare of the citizens and the individual's worth, ensuring one's obtainability.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

My country, Bangladesh, follows a mixed economic system. A comparative discussion:
Ownership: In a capitalist system (B), factors of production are privately owned. In Bangladesh's mixed economy, there is coexistence of private ownership and state ownership in key sectors.
Market Freedom: Capitalism promotes a free market with minimal government intervention. Bangladesh has a market economy but with significant government regulation and control in essential services and sectors.
Goal: The primary goal under capitalism is profit maximization. In Bangladesh's mixed system, goals include both economic growth (through private enterprise) and social welfare (through state intervention).
Labour Exploitation: Capitalism can lead to labour exploitation due to profit motive. In Bangladesh's mixed system, labour laws exist to protect workers, but exploitation can still occur in the private sector.
Resource Distribution: Capitalism often leads to unequal distribution of wealth. Bangladesh's mixed economy aims for a more balanced distribution through government policies, subsidies, and welfare programs, though inequality persists.

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is profit?","marks":1,"answer":"The money received by the owner is called profit.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why isn’t the sea-water called resource?","marks":2,"answer":"Since there is no scarcity of sea-water, it is not an asset. An asset is something that has utility, scarcity, transferability, and visibility. If a product does not have any one of these four qualities, it is not an asset. Since sea-water does not have scarcity, it is not an asset.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Give a description of the economic system of the country 'X'.","marks":3,"answer":"‘X’ country reflects capitalistic economic condition. Capitalism is the most prevalent economic system in the world today. A capitalist economy is an economic system in which individuals or private enterprises operate with the objective of maximizing profit. In the stem, it can be understood that a large portion of the people of the country 'X' is deprived of different facilities. Their income is low and demand is also very low. Their decision of purchasing is controlled by the market. Hence, the economic system of country 'X' is capitalistic. In this economic system, any person can take the initiative of producing any product or service. Hence, there are many producer and sellers in the market. There is unrestricted competition between them. The price of the product is determined through competition between the buyer and the seller. Investors often try to pay workers less than their fair wages in order to maximize profits. The investors keeps part of the wages as profit. As a result, discrimination is created in the distribution of produced wealth. A large number of workers of the society are deprived. Moreover, in the capitalistic economic system, there is freedom for the buyers. The buyers can take decisions about the quantity and type of goods. However, the decision can be controlled by choice, income and market price of the product. Therefore, country X reflects a capitalistic economic condition.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the relation of the economic system of Bangladesh with the economic system of the country 'Y'.","marks":4,"answer":"The economic condition of Bangladesh has both similarities and dissimilarities with the economic system of country Y, which follows the Islamic economic system. In country Y, the rich people donate money to the poor from their profits on a regular basis. This is why, the poor are not too poor. This is somewhat similar to the economic system that Bangladesh follows, which is a mixed economy. Mixed economic system is prevalent in Bangladesh. In this system, there is both governmental and non-governmental ownership. In the Islamic economic system, the individual ownership is prevalent. The wealth of individuals can be used according to own will. In the economy of Bangladesh, the personal property can be transferred to the successors. In the Islamic economic system, if an individual possess a certain amount of wealth for a certain time, then a part of it has to be distributed among the poor. This system is also prevalent in Bangladesh. Moreover, in Islamic economic system, due to following exploitation free production procedure, there is proper distribution of wealth and workers are paid enough. The workers are not deprived. On the other hand, in Bangladesh, there is partial distribution of income. A part of workers are deprived and exploited. As a result, discrimination is seen in income. From the above discussion it can be said that, there is both similarities and dissimilarities between the Islamic economic system mentioned in the 'Y' country and the mixed economic system of Bangladesh.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called utility?","marks":1,"answer":"The ability to meet human demands through any product is called utility.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the term insufficiency.","marks":2,"answer":"Insufficiency refers to the limitation of supply relative to demand. Insufficiency occurs when the supply of a good or service is less than the demand. For example, if the supply of rice is less than the demand for row in proportion to the specific population of an area, then it can be said that there is a insufficiency of rice in that ones. In this case, the consumer has to buy rice at a higher price to meet the demand.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"What is called the activity of Mr. Rahim in economics? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In economy, his work is called an organization. Organization is the management and execution of production by integrating the three factors of production, namely land, labor, and capital. The person who executes these is called a director. All risks or uncertainties in production are carried by the director. It is seen in the stem that Mr. Rahim buys diverse forms of wood from the market by taking loans from the bank. With some laborers, he shaped some tools like a roller for kneading and rolling tortillas, a chair, etc. Then he painted them and sold them in a rented shop in the market. That is, Mr. Rahim has put the people of the area as laborers in exchange for wages in the rented shop, considering it as land. And expenses, including buying wood, meaning that as capital he has taken a loan from the bank. That is, the tools, rollers, chairs, etc. are produced by integrating the factors of production, which are land, labor, and capital. That is why, his work can be called an organization.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Do you think that the activity of Mr. Rahim follows the proper distribution of income among the factors of production? Give reason in favour of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"Yes, I think, Mr. Rahim's work profit has been justifiably distributed among the elements. Distribution is the process of dividing the money received from the total productive assets into four components: rent, wages, interest, and profit. Rent are paid to the owner for the use of land in production. Similarly, wages are paid to the workers with interest to the owner of the capital and profit to the promoter. If these benefits, such as rent, wages, interest, and profit, are distributed fairly and appropriately among these components, economic activities speed up and economic welfare is achieved. In the stem, Mr. Rahim produced it by combining the ingredients of the product. He took the shop in exchange for rent as land. Taking some local people as employees and paying them a salary. And he himself made a profit or gain as a director, and in return for the capital, he is giving interest by paying the bank loan. Thus, wages, interest, and profits are properly distributed among the factors of production. Thus, it can be said from the above discussion that the profit from the work of Mr. Rahim has been distributed justifiably.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"How many divisions can the asset are divided into?","marks":1,"answer":"Resources or assets can be divided into four types—personal, collective, national and international.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What is the economic system? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The system or structure under which the ownership of factors of production is determined and the process of distribution and consumption of produced assets is accomplished is called the economic system. The system is formed combined with financial activities of the people and economic-related organizations and related structures. Four types of economic system are mainly effective in the present world: the capitalist, the socialist, the mixed and the Islamic economic systems.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the nature of the economic system of the country 'A' of Pertho from the point of view of the subject matter you learnt.","marks":3,"answer":"In the state 'A' of Pertho in the stem, the socialist economic system is present. The main objective of the socialist economic system is to ensure rights of all through removing discriminations in the production and distribution systems. No private ownership is vested on the factors of production in this economic system. Factors of production, investment, distribution, etc. are run in a planned way under the control of the state. In the socialist economic system, the state integrates the four factors of production and gives guidance to the production activities. There is no scope here for making a personal profit. Therefore, economic activities cannot be under anyone's personal control. In the stem, Pertho is a citizen of the state 'A', where the characteristic of the socialist economic system of not establishing any industry under a private initiative has been reflected. Besides, the factory where Pertho's father works gives him part of his due wage as needed. Therefore, it can be said that the socialist economic system exists in the country 'A' of the stem.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Discuss with logic the difference between the economic systems of the country 'B' with the economic system of country 'A'.","marks":4,"answer":"There are a few basic dissimilarities between the capitalist economic system in the state 'B' and the socialist economic system in the state 'A'. The capitalist and socialist economic systems develop with two different types of ideologies. One encourages personal initiatives and profit while another ensures proper wages of the labourers and the maintain control of the state. In the stem, it is seen that Pertho is a citizen of the state 'A' and though there is no freedom of running any private initiative in that country a balanced distribution system in production has been ensured there. Afterwards, he became a citizen of a country where the capitalist economic system exists. Pertho established factories in the country, as personal initiatives are encouraged there. In the capitalist economic system, the components such as land, labourers, capital and organization remain under the private ownership. On the other hand, all assets remain under the state ownership in the socialist economic system. In the capitalist economic system, any individual can make wealth by producing any goods or providing any service, establishing factories and doing business activities at will. Besides, in the capitalist economic system, which goods and what quantity of it will be consumed by an individual is decided by himself. He makes the decision according to his preference, income and market price of the commodity. On the contrary, in a socialist country, the government decides which goods will be produced in what quantity and when and in what process the goods will be sold to whom. The government produces and imports goods as per the need of the society in the socialist economic system. Therefore, the consumer does not have any freedom here. According to the above statement, it can be said that the two economic systems mentioned in the stem have some basic differences.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

The prevalence of a mixed economic system in Bangladesh, like in country ‘Kha’, is noticeable. A financial system in which private and public enterprises coexist is called a mixed economic system. In this system, private ownership and private enterprise, as well as full or partial government ownership, initiative, and control, are effective in some sectors. This system includes the recognition of private ownership in the production, investment, and consumption of goods, which is characteristic of a capitalist economy. Again, in a mixed economy, consumers can exercise freedom in buying, selling, and consuming goods. In the production and consumption of goods in Bangladesh, this picture is also different. Hence, from the above discussion it can be stated that, among the two countries in the country ‘Kha’, there is mixed economic system. In this economic system, an individual can enjoy his/her wealth or property according to own will. Moreover, the necessary products and services for the normal people are managed by the government.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is labour?","marks":1,"answer":"The physical and mental ability of people that can be used in production is called labour.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Japan called high-income country?","marks":2,"answer":"As the per capita income of Japan is 12276 or more, it can be called a high-income country. Per capita is the main indicator of a country’s economic development and standard of living. It is determined whether the country is developed or underdeveloped through this. The World Bank has divided the countries of the world into three main categories based on gross national income. In this regard, Japan is known as a high-income country as the per capita income of Japan is 39030 US Dollars.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which type of asset is the house of the stem? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In the stem, the house belonging to Mr. M is personal asset on the basis of ownership. Resources can be divided into 4 classes – personal, collective, national and international. Personally owned land, house, factory, money, car, good, etc. are called personal assets. Although own intellect and personal skills are non-transferable, but an individual can create resources utilizing those qualities. So, these are included within personal assets. In the stem, we can see that Mr. M buys 10 bighas of land and builds a shelter for the elderly people. He has his own authority over the house. That means, he manages the house personally. So, it can be said that on the basis of ownership, the house belonging to Mr. M is a personal asset.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"What should we do to preserve the asset as mentioned at the end of the stem? Give opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"The last resource in the stem is a collective resource. We need to perform various actions in order to preserve this resource. All personal resources of citizens of a country and the collective resources of the society are jointly called national resources. In this case, the resources that people collectively own are collective resources; it also includes natural and manufactured resources owned by the state. The state and the people collectively own these resources. The people of the country use and enjoy the collective wealth. Through the planned use of these, the state takes measures for the overall development and welfare of the people. The need for everyone’s awareness and initiative to preserve the country’s resources is immense. In this case, citizens should be aware and diligent about their duties. Along with this, it is important to have clear instructions in the documents of the organization about the responsibilities and duties of the organization assigned to preserve and supervise them. In the stem, it can be seen that a man tries to steal the slippers from a railway track next to Mr. M’s house. In a brave attempt, Mr. M tries to stop him. parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is an organization?","marks":1,"answer":"The management and execution of the production activities related to the three factors of production namely—land, labour and capital is called organization.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why isn’t the air a resource in economics?","marks":2,"answer":"Air is not considered a resource in economics because of its abundance, invisibility and non-transferability. In economics, wealth refers to things that have utility, scarcity, visibility and transferability. In this case, utility is the ability to meet the need. Scarcity refers to the limitation of supply compared to demand. Visibility is the appearance of things. And transferability is the possibility of one person getting the object from another person. Air has utility. But air is infinite in nature. Therefore, there is no scarcity of it. It is not visible and cannot be transferred. For this reason air is not a resource in the economy.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the economic system which is existing in country ‘X’ mentioned in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The country ‘X’ mentioned in the state has an Islamic economic system. The Islamic economic system is based on Shariah principles. It allows private ownership and free market operations but with moral and religious guidelines. Zakat is compulsory, which ensures wealth redistribution to the poor. In this system, production and consumption are guided by Islamic laws, and exploitation is prohibited.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Is the same type of laborer exploitation existed in both countries mentioned in the stem? Give logic in favour of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"No, both countries do not have the same kind of labour exploitation. The country ‘X’ mentioned in the stem has an Islamic economic system and the country ‘Y’ has a mixed economic system. Between mixed and Islamic economy, workers are not exploited in Islamic economy. On the other hand, competition is high in mixed economic systems. At the same time, there is partial exploitation of workers due to the aim of achieving profit. In Islamic economy, non-exploitative production process is followed. In this, there is a fair distribution of wealth and workers get fair pay. In this system, the worker's dues are paid on time. On the other hand, in mixed economy there is partial fair distribution of wealth or income. And workers in particular are exploited and deprived. As a result, income inequality is noticeable. Interest is prohibited in Islamic economy while interest-based transactions are allowed in mixed economy. Another major welfare aspect of Islamic economy is the system of Zakat. The rich are obliged to donate a portion of their wealth to the poor. Based on the above discussion, it can be said that between the mixed economy and the Islamic economy, the Islamic economy ensures better welfare of the society and the state; committed to fair payment of workers. There is no such thing as labour exploitation in Islamic economy.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Resources in economics refer to things that have utility, scarcity, visibility and transferability. Utility in this case is the ability to fill a deficiency. Scarcity refers to the limitation of supply compared to demand. Visibility is the externality of things. And transferability is the possibility of getting the object from one person to another. That is why, sunlight is not a resource in the economy.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which economic system is present in country 'A?' In a socialist economy, the state owns all resources, including the means of production. There is no individual ownership of assets. All products are produced by state enterprises. In this financial system, there is no opportunity to produce any goods personally. It can also be seen that there is no opportunity to establish any industry by private initiative in country 'B.' In the stem, Badhon goes to country ‘B’ and observes that no organization can be established through a private initiative. All the decisions of the country's production system are taken by the government. These features of the country's economic system indicate the socialist system. In a socialist economic system, production activities are conducted to meet the basic needs of the people and maximize public welfare. It is the state that provides work and fair wages to the workers according to their merits. No one is deprived of the income according to his merit in production. As a result, workers are not exploited and wealth is not concentrated in the hands of a capitalist. For these reasons, there is a fair distribution of wealth. From the discussion above, it can be said that in the socialist economic system, as there is no opportunity for private initiative and the state provides work and wages to everyone according to their abilities and qualifications, the workers are not exploited by the capitalists in socialist economic system.\n---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

The resources that the people of the country may collectively use are called collective resources. Citizens have equal rights over such resources and equal responsibility for them. Roads, railways, dams, parks, government hospitals, and schools are covered by collective wealth. Besides, state-owned forests, mineral resources, rivers, etc. are also examples of collective resources. In the stem, it has been told, Mr. Amin saw two to three people illegally cutting forest trees. He stopped cutting trees with the help of the villagers. That is, he saved the collective wealth. Collective resources are used and enjoyed by people. Through the planned use of these resources, the state provides for the development and welfare of the people. These resources are very valuable. In some cases, resources are limited. Due to this, if they are used in an unplanned manner, there may be a resource crisis in the country. So every citizen needs to take special care to conserve the collective wealth. The individual and collective wealth of a country's citizens together is considered national wealth. In this case, the resources that the people collectively own are collective resources; they also include natural and manufactured resources owned by the state. The state and the people collectively own these resources. The collective resources are used and enjoyed by the people of the state. Through the planned use of these, the state takes measures for the overall development and welfare of the people. The need for collective awareness and initiatives to conserve the country's resources is immense. Citizens should be aware and diligent about their duties to preserve the collective and national resources of the country. Also, it is important to have clear instructions in the documents of the organization about the responsibilities and duties of the organization assigned to preserve and supervise them. By doing this, the officers and employees of the organization can perform their proper duties, and their supervision is also easy. Mr. Amin of the stem stopped the illegal cutting of forest trees with the help of villagers. But to preserve such resources the above mentioned steps should be taken.
